Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Longitudinal ATAC/CUT&Tag after transient stimulus
ideas.description: Expose cells (e.g., fibroblasts, macrophages, or keratinocytes) to a transient stimulus such as TPA, TNF, or wounding. Then map AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding and chromatin accessibility at days to weeks after washout, and test whether AP-1-motif enhancers remain open or primed, and whether they drive faster transcription on restimulation than in naïve cells.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation during the memory phase
ideas.description: Use dTAG/auxin-inducible degrons or dominant-negative A-FOS to remove AP-1 either during the initial stimulus or only after it ends. If memory requires AP-1 only for establishment, degradation in the maintenance phase should leave it intact. If AP-1 is needed for maintenance, memory should decay. Read out restimulation response, accessibility, and H3K27ac.

ideas.title: Single-cell live imaging of AP-1 dynamics and memory
ideas.description: Track AP-1 reporters or endogenously tagged FOS/JUN in single cells through repeated stimulation pulses. Quantify whether the history of past pulses predicts later response amplitude and kinetics, and whether the response is heritable across cell divisions in sister cells, to separate true memory from cell-to-cell heterogeneity.

ideas.title: Sufficiency test with synthetic AP-1 induction and optogenetics
ideas.description: Drive AP-1 activity with a controlled optogenetic or chemogenetic c-Jun/c-Fos system without upstream signaling. Then test whether a pulse alone creates durable accessibility and a primed transcriptional response at endogenous loci. Vary pulse duration and frequency to define the dose and timing thresholds for memory.

ideas.title: Perturbing chromatin cofactors and in vivo memory models
ideas.description: Test whether AP-1 memory depends on partner factors such as BAF/SWI-SNF, p300, or pioneer factors. Inhibit or deplete them after the initial stimulus, and use CUT&Tag and Micro-C to track enhancer-promoter contacts. Validate in vivo, for example with repeated skin injury or inflammatory challenge, by lineage tracing and by comparing a primary to a secondary response.
